respondent:
State of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

21 June 2007
Appeal (crl.) 833 of 2007

statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The appellants, Shaikah Bakshu and others, challenged a judgment of the Bombay High Court, Aurangabad Bench.
Rubina was married to appellant No.1 Sk. Bakshu about 8 days prior to the alleged incident, which took place on 19.8.2001 at about 4 p.m. in the house of the appellants.

The prosecution version as unfolded during trial is that Rubina was caught hold of by her mother-in-law and sister-in-law while her husband, Sk. Bakshu, poured kerosene on her person, set her on fire.
The deceased suffered burn injuries and was taken to the Civil Hospital, Parbhani, where she died at 8-30 p.m. on 19.8.2001.
The investigation of the case was conducted by Anil Gaikwad (PW-6), who drew spot panchnama and recorded statements of witnesses.
issues: Whether the dying declarations were credible and cogent
Whether the prosecution had concocted a false case
petitioner_arguments: The appellants denied the incident in question and alleged that the witnesses were demanding money and for that reason, they are deposing falsely.
The alleged place of occurrence has been differently stated.
No explanation has been offered as to why there was necessity of recording two dying declarations.
respondent_arguments: After analyzing the evidence in detail conviction has been recorded.
The trial court and High Court held that the dying declaration was credible because the medical officer was present when the dying declaration was recorded.
court_reasoning: The trial court accepted this position to be correct from the record, but made a new case that the time recorded to be 6.30 p.m. appears to be a mistake made by ASI.
The High Court concluded that even though it is not so stated, it has to be presumed that [the dying declaration] was read over and explained.
holding: Conviction for offence relatable to Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC was maintained.
Acquittal was recorded under Section 498-A read with Section 34 IPC.
